children: Export sales of U.S. soybeans landed on the low side of analyst forecasts for the week, according to data from the Department of Agriculture.

In its weekly export sales report published Thursday, the USDA said that for the week ended Sept. 17, soybean export sales for the 2026/27 marketing year totaled 582,400 metric tons. Analysts surveyed by The Wall Street Journal this week had forecast sales to land between 500,000 tons and 2 million tons.
Corn sales for the week totaled 838,300 tons, while wheat sales were 267,600 tons. Both totals are on the lower end of analyst forecasts for the week.
CBOT grain futures are mixed in pre-market trading Thursday. Most-active corn futures are down 0.3%, while soybeans are up 0.3% and wheat is 0.7% lower.
To see related data, search "U.S. Export Sales: Weekly Sales Totals" in Dow Jones NewsPlus.
